correctness.rationale: For any finite nonempty labeled open unit-interval family of ply <=2, if left endpoints a_i are sorted, an overlap of indices i<j with j>=i+2 implies simultaneous coverage by interval i+1, violating ply two. The overlap graph is thus disjoint consecutive paths; nonneighbor disjointness forces their sorted order. Two adjacent inversions would invert nonneighbors, so realizable permutations are exactly products of disjoint adjacent swaps. Conversely the point choice p_{pi(t)}=max_{u<=t}a_{pi(u)}+t epsilon realizes every permutation respecting disjoint interval order. For a path, W_1=1, W_m=W_(m-1) m (m-1) contains all matching-swap permutations, while any common word either uses >=2 copies of m or a unique final-ish m with both universal prefix and a required later m-1, forcing length >=2m-1. Projection onto components proves OPT=2n-c and Fibonacci matching counts. Independently enumerated path targets and BFS minima for n=1..5: (1,3,5,7,9); correct n=1 and coincident-pair boundary. The finite BFS alone does not prove the general lemma.
